metadata.title: Claude, Financial Statements.
metadata.purpose: Answer whether Claude applies its own accounting judgment when it flags a variance as material, using the financial-statements skill's own documented mechanism as the case. Lands the carry-out that flagging a variance is a rule checked from a written file, not judgment Claude applies on the fly.
metadata.anchor_pair: B02 -> B03 (the 'financial statements - Q1' request, submitted, walked through the same steps, run twice, then Q2)

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes Claude uses its own judgment to decide what counts as a material variance. It doesn't. It checks numbers against rules written in a file, every time. What's in that file?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'Claude decides what's a material variance. Right?', hesitates on 'decides', corrects to 'checks', lands the real question

props.text:
Claude decides
what's a
material variance.
Right?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('decides' -> 'checks') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: Open the financial-statements folder and there's no separate module for accounting judgment. One file, SKILL.md, spells out the job: build the income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow statement, compare each period to the last, and flag variances that cross a threshold the file itself sets. Claude reads that instruction and follows it — nothing is left to discretion.

shot.new_visual_element: A folder opens onto one file, SKILL.md, listing its job in plain language; no second 'judgment' module anywhere

production_viz.label: No separate judgment module — one file spells out the job
production_viz.mechanic: A folder icon opens onto a single tile: SKILL.md. Its job unrolls in plain language beside it: three statement names, 'compare periods', 'flag variances over threshold'. A second, empty slot labelled 'ACCOUNTING JUDGMENT' appears then is struck through — nothing there.

beats.narration_text: The pipeline lives in the Steps section, and Claude works through it top to bottom — linear, no branching unless a step says so. Ask for financial statements covering the first quarter, and it builds the income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow, lines each one up against the prior period, and flags what crosses the threshold — the same steps, every single time.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — a 'financial statements · Q1' request goes in, ordered steps light up in sequence, an output card (three statements + flags) comes out

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — request in, steps in order, statements + flags out
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. A request card 'financial statements · Q1' enters from the left. Four numbered step tiles light up left to right, one at a time, never out of order (build statements, compare periods, flag variances, return output). An output card labelled 'Q1 — INCOME / BALANCE / CASH FLOW, 1 FLAGGED' appears on the right. THIS EXACT REQUEST AND STEP SEQUENCE RETURN AT B03.

beats.narration_text: Ask for that same first-quarter statement again, and the flags come back identical — not because Claude re-judged the numbers, but because the same steps ran a second time. That cuts both ways: identical flags on identical input isn't proof Claude understood the business, it only proves the fixed steps repeated. And a different flag showing up next quarter doesn't mean the rule changed either — the same steps just ran against new numbers.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — the same Q1 request submitted twice, two identical output cards; beside it, a Q2 request producing a different card from the same steps

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — same input twice, then a different one
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 REQUEST RETURNS, identical, run through the same four step tiles again. Two 'Q1 — 1 FLAGGED' output cards sit side by side, character-for-character identical. Beside them, a third run: 'financial statements · Q2' enters the same steps and exits as a visibly different output card ('Q2 — 2 FLAGGED'). A caption beneath: 'same steps, every time — the input is what changes.'

beats.narration_text: Flagging a variance isn't Claude's judgment call — it checks the numbers against a rule someone already wrote, the same way every single time.

props.quote: Flagging a variance isn't Claude's judgment call — it checks the numbers against a rule someone already wrote, the same way every single time.
props.sparkLine: A written rule. Not a judgment call.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Open the financial-statements skill folder. Before you run anything, read me the SKILL.md and tell me, in your own words, what makes a variance count as material. Liam, in for Bear.
